summary_out.hypothesis: Loop-5's next directive named posting one tick inside the touch to trade fill-rate against price improvement; the bet was that a price one tick closer to the mid is hit by enough extra flow (the marginal flow trading through the first tick of depth) that fewer orders fall through to the +half_spread market fallback, and that fill-rate gain would outweigh the +1-tick-worse IS cost paid on each passive fill.
summary_out.next: The hypothesis was wrong — the +1-tick per-fill IS penalty is deterministic on every passive fill while the fill-rate gain is marginal, so moving the limit toward the mid strictly worsens aggregate IS. This establishes the IS-optimal passive resting price within loop-5's structure is AT the touch (inside_ticks=0), and loop-6 is the empirical proof that inside_ticks=1 < inside_ticks=0. The remaining untried execution-objective lever is the OTHER direction loop-5 named: tune passive_timeout_ms — a longer window converts market-fallback orders into loop-5-quality at-the-touch passive fills (no per-fill price penalty) at the cost of signal staleness / adverse selection. P&L remains unmovable by any execution-side choice under sigma=200; a future loop wanting positive P&L must change WHICH orders enter the fill set correlated with forward-return sign, which equity-feedback (loops 1-2) and book-imbalance (loop 3) already failed to do.
